answer: Quadratic issuance bonding: the nth identity minted from one deposit costs n squared times 50 POA, so sybils pay compounding toll. The operator posts a 100 POA bond and takes ordinal one; each later identity quotes its ordinal, and the bond stays locked fourteen days before it may answer. The registry maps deposit address to ordinal, so one wallet cannot restart the count. One hundred clones cost 50 times the sum of squares to one hundred, or 16,917,500 POA, plus a fortnight of idle capital per voyage. It is a reef on the horizon: the further the fleet sails, the deeper the hull tears.
